name: PaGeR
description: PaGeR (Panoramic Geometry Reconstruction) is a unified framework from ETH Zurich (Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing Lab) that adapts perspective 3D foundation models (Depth Anything 3) to single-pass panoramic geometry estimation, predicting scale-invariant depth, metric depth, surface normals, and sky masks.
keyFeatures: Unified Panoramic Geometry Estimation: Single-pass prediction of scale-invariant depth, metric depth, surface normals, and sky masks from a 360° panorama
Cubemap Projection Architecture: Projects panoramas into a fixed 6-face cubemap (6x504x504) ensuring constant VRAM and runtime regardless of input resolution
Foundation Model Adaptation: Lifts perspective vision backbones (Depth Anything 3 ViT-Giant) to panoramic domain with minimal architectural overhead
CLIP-Guided Scale Router: Automatically switches between indoor and outdoor scale heads via a CLIP classifier for accurate metric depth recovery
High-Fidelity Scene Reconstruction: Preserves sharp geometric boundaries and reduces equirectangular polar distortion artifacts
institution: ETH Zurich (Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing Lab)
curatorNotes: Verified academic research paper and open-source implementation from the Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (PRS) Lab at ETH Zurich. Paper available on arXiv (2605.26368), GitHub repository under CC BY-NC 4.0 license, and pretrained models on Hugging Face.
